title: METOC Senior Forecaster (MGySgt to Cpl) NMOS (6842), DC I
raw_text:
3.     MOS 6862, METOC Senior Forecaster (MGySgt to Cpl) NMOS (6842), DC I

    a. Summary. Senior Meteorology and Oceanography (METOC) Forecasters
predict environmental conditions and the effects of these forecasted
conditions in support of the MAGTF platforms and operations. These Senior
Forecasters serve as a team leader and senior instructors (SI) within
reference (af), Meteorology and Oceanography Training and Readiness Manual.
Senior METOC Forecasters are proficient in the use of environmental sensors
and plans which characterize the physical environment. This MOS is assigned
only as an NMOS to qualified METOC Forecasters.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must hold MOS 6842.

        (2) Security requirement: must have a current single scope
background investigation/T5 investigation and adjudicated for sensitive
compartmented information (SCI) eligibility.

    c. Requirements. Complete the Aerographer’s Mate Class C1 Course
(F02WBF2) at MARDET Keesler AFB, MS.

    d. Duties. For a complete list of duties and tasks, refer to MCRP 2-
10B.6, MAGTF Meteorological and Oceanographic Operations and NAVMC 3500.38,
Meteorological and Oceanographic Training and Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
All Other 25-3099.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   METOC Analyst Forecaster, 6842.

SERVICES 1. Introduction. The Meteorological and Oceanographic (METOC) Services OccFld is responsible for collecting, assessing, and disseminating environmental data, information, and intelligence, relevant to friendly and enemy force strengths and vulnerabilities for the planning and execution of operations necessary to characterize the battle space. This includes atmospheric, space, climatic, hydrologic, and littoral oceanographic information for use in the production of Tactical Decision Aids (TDA) and METOC effects matrices. The METOC OccFld is comprised of 6842 METOC Analyst Forecaster, 6891 METOC Chief, and 6802 METOC Services Officer. Marines entering the 6800 OccFld will complete formal training and receive MOS 6842. As their skill enhancing training progresses, they become eligible to attend MOSs 6852, 6862, and 6877 instruction.

3. MOS 6862, METOC Senior Forecaster (MGySgt to Cpl) NMOS (6842), DC I a. Summary. Senior Meteorology and Oceanography (METOC) Forecasters predict environmental conditions and the effects of these forecasted conditions in support of the MAGTF platforms and operations. These Senior Forecasters serve as a team leader and senior instructors (SI) within reference (af), Meteorology and Oceanography Training and Readiness Manual. Senior METOC Forecasters are proficient in the use of environmental sensors and plans which characterize the physical environment. This MOS is assigned only as an NMOS to qualified METOC Forecasters. b. Prerequisites (1) Must hold MOS 6842. (2) Security requirement: must have a current single scope background investigation/T5 investigation and adjudicated for sensitive compartmented information (SCI) eligibility. c. Requirements. Complete the Aerographer’s Mate Class C1 Course (F02WBF2) at MARDET Keesler AFB, MS. d. Duties. For a complete list of duties and tasks, refer to MCRP 2- 10B.6, MAGTF Meteorological and Oceanographic Operations and NAVMC 3500.38, Meteorological and Oceanographic Training and Readiness Manual.

matches: Gather data from sources such as surface or upper air stations, satellites, weather bureaus, or radar for use in meteorological reports or forecasts.

The Meteorological and Oceanographic (METOC) Services OccFld is responsible for collecting, assessing, and disseminating environmental data, information, and intelligence, relevant to friendly and enemy force strengths and vulnerabilities for the planning and execution of operations necessary to characterize the battle space.
Compile and evaluate hydrologic information to prepare navigational charts and maps and to predict atmospheric conditions.
This includes atmospheric, space, climatic, hydrologic, and littoral oceanographic information for use in the production of Tactical Decision Aids (TDA) and METOC effects matrices.
Interpret weather and vessel conditions to determine appropriate responses.
Senior Meteorology and Oceanography (METOC) Forecasters predict environmental conditions and the effects of these forecasted conditions in support of the MAGTF platforms and operations.
Develop and deliver training on weather topics.
These Senior Forecasters serve as a team leader and senior instructors (SI) within reference (af), Meteorology and Oceanography Training and Readiness Manual.
Interpret data, reports, maps, photographs, or charts to predict long- or short-range weather conditions, using computer models and knowledge of climate theory, physics, and mathematics.
Senior METOC Forecasters are proficient in the use of environmental sensors and plans which characterize the physical environment.
Complete and maintain records of weather and beach conditions, emergency medical treatments performed, and other relevant incident information.
For a complete list of duties and tasks, refer to MCRP 2- 10B.6, MAGTF Meteorological and Oceanographic Operations and NAVMC 3500.38, Meteorological and Oceanographic Training and Readiness Manual.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
